question: Why must you profile a Markdown documentation corpus before designing your RAG chunking pipeline?
options: Because Python cannot read Markdown files without counting words first
Because structural features like heading hierarchies and pipe tables (950+ rows in sarvam-docs) determine whether naive fixed-window splitting will corrupt tables and lose section context
Because BigQuery charges per Markdown heading
To convert all tables into audio files
explanation: Profiling reveals high table and heading density in sarvam-docs, showing why structure-aware Markdown chunking is required instead of naive character slicing.

question: What is the safest way to log environment configuration during RAG service startup?
options: Commit .env to a public GitHub branch so teammates can see it
Mask sensitive keys (such as HF_TOKEN) so only a short prefix/suffix or length is shown, and keep .env in .gitignore
Encode API keys in Base64 and print them in full
explanation: Deterministic secret masking prevents accidental credential exposure in terminal logs, CI outputs, and monitoring systems.

question: How many Markdown documents and approximately how many words make up the sarvam-docs developer corpus?
options: 64 documents and ~58,284 words across api-reference/ and documentation/
explanation: The sarvam-docs corpus contains 64 Markdown files totaling 58,284 words across 36 API reference specs, 27 developer guides, and 1 root README.

question: Which command configures Google Cloud Application Default Credentials (ADC) so Python SDKs (Vertex AI, BigQuery, GCS) authenticate without hardcoded service-account JSON files?
explanation: gcloud auth application-default login stores local user credentials in a standard location automatically discovered by google-cloud-* and google-genai Python libraries.
